column3: NKJV capitalizes “He” and “Him,” reads “before Him” of God, and renders the future “He shall grow up.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a man of pains” is rendered “A Man of sorrows,” and “sickness” “grief.”
Close to the Hebrew; “sicknesses… pains” is rendered “griefs… sorrows.”
Close to the Hebrew; “pierced” is rendered “wounded,” “crushed” “bruised,” and “wound[s]” “stripes.”
Close to the Hebrew; “sheep… ewe” is rendered “lamb… sheep.”
Close to the Hebrew; “from oppression” is rendered “from prison,” “consider” “declare,” and “a wound to him” “He was stricken.”
Close to the Hebrew; “one assigned” is rendered “they made,” and NKJV adds “But” before “with the rich.”
NKJV reads “if it/you make” as second person, “When You make His soul an offering for sin,” and renders “guilt offering” as “an offering for sin.”
NKJV follows the MT without “light,” “He shall see the labor of His soul,” and capitalizes “My righteous Servant.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the many… mighty” is rendered “the great… the strong,” and “will make entreaty” “made intercession.”
